newsitem.title: UK: Emirates ex-UK cargo up 21pct in year to March 97.
newsitem.headline: Emirates ex-UK cargo up 21pct in year to March 97.

text.p: Emirates' ex-UK cargo tonnage flown in the financial year to end-March 1997 was 21 percent up on the previous year's total, said its UK cargo marketing controller Jacqui Evans.
She declined to give details of the figures, but added that tonnage flown from Ireland during 1996-97 was up 65 percent on the previous year.
"We are at the high end of the cargo rate scale but this growth shows the success we are achieving by offering a quality product," she said.

The Dubai government-owned airline currently offers 75 tonnes of ex-UK cargo capacity each day -- on twice-daily ex-London Heathrow to Dubai Boeing 777-200 flights and respective daily Airbus A310 services from London Gatwick and Manchester.
Mohamed Qasim Al Ali, Emirates' UK and Ireland general manager, said cargo capacity was restricted because of high passenger loads from Britain to Dubai at this time of the year.
"But with four flights a day ex-UK, there is still plenty more room to take on more cargo," he said.
